title: Fairgrounds picnics: brass bands, upstairs bands and the Eagle Band
summary: At fairground picnics brass bands played marches and waltzes downstairs, other bands on the stairs, and the Eagle Band played blues in the field.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Now, what about the different time signatures they used to use there? Would they play much six-eighths music and dances?

No, I mean, when they had the picnics, like at the fairground, I mean, well, that was a different story. You see the picnics at the fairground, when they had, like the bulls would give a picnic, a lion or the two-layer, the Aiden Social Pleasure Club. One of those would give a picnic, you know. At the fairground, well, they'd have three bands, you see. Downstairs, in the big hall, they'd have the, either the Excelsior Brass Band or the OBBs, the Ormond Brass Band, see. And they'd play, they'd play the marches. The six-eighths, and they'd play the waltzes. And on the, then when you're going upstairs, and like you're going to the grandstand upstairs, I mean, well, in between the stairs, they'd have another band. Maybe a John Robichaud's band, or Emmanuel Peres's band, or one of those bands. And then way out in the field, way out in the field, in the middle of the field, well, that was the Hunky Tonk. Well, they always did have the Eagle Band. The Eagle Band was a blues band, a Valhaut's band, see. Frank Aducer's band, Bob Lyon and them, see. That was, that was for all the ratty people, you know. All the people want to be in the dark and, and dance the way they want to, you know, dance the way they want to dance, you know. You know, they want to, who don't shake, don't get no kick on those things, you know. Well, they was way out in the field. They was by theyself out there, all along by theyself, see.
Well, what sort of deal did they have set up in the field? Would they have a bar out there or something? Well, yeah, they had all that, no, they had all that, yeah, they had a little bar out there.
They had no big bar, because a big bar would be in a place where the, where the big branch band was playing, either Seltzer or the one with branch band playing, see.
Would they have a roof out there or anything?
No, no, just, just, just like it is today. You know, the horses running around the track, well, in that center, in that.
I thought maybe they set up a tent or something.
No, no, no, no, no tent, nothing. It was a barrel house. I don't know why this, I mean, it's like a tent.
Big watch tub out there. I was wondering about some tune like Gettysburg, when you'd play that at a dance in those days.

Well, those bands, the brass band played that, you see, they played all the nice tunes, you see, you know. The good class of people, I mean, they stayed right there and danced by the big band, you see. Well, the band on the, on the, on the steps, well, the people, well, it was pretty good, you know, pretty good music, too, you know. But, you know, it wasn't classy as, wait, make it this straight. People downstairs that danced by the big band. All those people, you know, all those, liking people in society, you know, they all want to be nice and dance nice, see. Well, the band on the stairs, well, those people just danced or never danced, you know, like they wanted to dance. But the barrel horse people went out in the field. Now, did you get my point? That's the best I could be playing. Yeah, I got it. I got it, yeah. Yeah. So that's that.
Yeah. Now, the brass band, would it play in two four, four four, three four?
Yeah, they played two four, two four, yeah, they played a lot of two four, and played a lot of marches.
Six eight.
Six eight, yeah, that's six eight. And they played a lot of waltzes. A lot of waltzes, beautiful, too.
They played four four, anything four four?
Yeah, they played four four, yeah, they played four four.
Now, what about upstairs? They'd have Robichaud out there, one of those bands.

Robichaud, you know, Imperial Band or Superior, one of those bands, you know what I mean? Well, they played like Maple Leaf Rag and, you know, African Pass and Grayson Buter and, you know, Field Rag, all the tunes, and maybe some popular tunes at that particular time, you know? But that band, that Frankie Deuce's band, they had a low band, that's what you call a low band.
They always hired them to play out in the field.
Nobody else played out there. Eagle Band, that was Eagle Band.
